body:
# Adversarial audit of body-tied attainment, actual cover, and one separator

Sources read in full:

- `candidate 26455afca6af9c16`
- `candidate 8effe5eb4947ba88`

The audit also read the actual compact-minimal-base, dependence/diameter,
finite clipping, energy-supergradient, signed-energy-envelope, and
outside-support inverse/separator dependencies cited below.


for the actual conservative response cone. I found no missing geometric
realization, interchange of infima, or change of separator between tests.
There is one harmless but real scope correction to the displayed bound
f_H<=1, and an explicit compact coefficient-space construction should
be retained when writing the finite-intersection proof. Neither requires
a new mathematical hypothesis. No numerical Gamma payment follows.

## 1. What is conditional in attainment

The fixed base must satisfy the ORIGINAL-depth minimal-bad hypotheses in
`candidate f7c05b2c30c8cfcb`, Section 1:
dependence-connectedness, equality of representation-preserving arrays
with affine arrays, a strict original bad sublevel, and the proper-closed-
minor lower bounds after their canonical lifts. The new buffer does not
prove these hypotheses and does not need a buffered minor inequality.

Under those inputs the mass-floor argument is valid before any shape
compactness. If a sequence lost a fiber's mass, its positive limiting
support T would be closed by the actual anchored inclusions; restriction
and canonical-lift transfer give beta_0>=M_T Gamma_d/k(T), contradicting
the fixed bad sublevel as M_T tends to one. Thus all sampled masses have
a positive uniform floor.

The diameter propagation in
`candidate dbf3b23d25004153` uses a bounded,
positive-volume source copy actually contained in each target, and a
fixed finite family of positive representations. Connectedness propagates
one normalized shape bound. The representation matrix then bounds the
centroid array modulo representation-preserving translations; the latter
are actual base-affine shears by the fixed-base hypothesis. Hence the
compact class really represents the whole original bad sublevel. It is
not an artificial ball constraint on the new variational problem.

Positive sampled volumes and a common outer ball also supply uniform
inradii and covariance eigenvalue floors by compactness. Compatibility,
positive volume, and original depth continuity survive the Hausdorff
limit. The new f_H is invariant under precisely the normalizing maps.
A minimizing sequence whose new value is below b therefore lies in this
same compact class after normalization and attains its infimum.

## 2. Uniformity of depth continuity and source cores

Normalizing a nonvertical normal by |u|=1 leaves arbitrary base tilts,
but its threshold change under a mark/body perturbation is bounded by
|delta y| plus the uniform change in epsilon f_H Gamma. This bound is
independent of the base tilt. Total symmetric-difference mass plus the
common slab bound controls ALL nonvertical caps at once. Pure-base caps
select finitely many whole-fiber subsets, including their closed boundary
fibers. Taking infima and subsequent maxima is consequently legitimate.

At least one sampled fiber has volume >=1/|P|. Its ordinary centroid
supplies an ordinary mixed lower depth Gamma_d/|P|, since every containing
ambient cap contains the corresponding own-fiber cap. Own-boundary depth
is zero by the finite support-height LP, not by a claim about arbitrary
real slice roofs. The uniform own-mark Lipschitz estimate then puts all
ordinary deepest marks in a common core. The O(epsilon) depth comparison
puts all buffered deepest marks in a slightly smaller common core.

The projective energy on a centered inball is its volume, so energy
monotonicity gives the stated positive source floor. The shift of each
nonvertical through-source plane includes an own-ball strip of uniformly
positive section area and width bounded below by a fixed multiple of
epsilon. For a pure-base minimizing cap, opposite infinitesimal continuous
tilts split its boundary fibers; one captures at most half their total
mass. Thus its reserve over ordinary depth is at least V_p/2. This closes
the infimum over both cap types and proves the uniform linear value gap.
It also gives the buffered pure-base gap and actual own properness.

For scale selection choose epsilon_bar<=1, harmlessly. A near-minimizer
whose penalized value is below b then has beta_0<b. The penalty prevents
epsilon tending to zero at fixed tau, while the linear lower and upper
value gaps give epsilon_tau/tau bounded above and below. Hence selected
scales are eventually interior. No free-parameter compactness was imported.

## 3. One scope correction: the bound f_H<=1 is sampled

For sampled z, E_z<=V_z<=M gives f_H<=(V_z/M)^(1/d)<=1.
For a REAL intermediate base of the canonical hull, V_z can exceed M.
Therefore the final <=1 in equation (2) of the body-tied note should be
explicitly restricted to sampled bases. This does not affect its cap error,
source-core, response, or floor estimates, all of which use sampled marks.
On the full real canonical hull f_H is still continuous, concave, and
bounded by a uniform compact-class constant.

Here is an exact example even on a dependence-connected complete base.
In Z^2 let p1=(1,0), p2=(0,1), p3=(-1,-1), p0=(0,0). These are exactly
the integer points of their triangle. In continuous dimension two use
centered rectangles with half-widths

    K_p1: (100,1), K_p2: (1,100), K_p3: (1,1),
    K_p0: (34,34).

The last rectangle is exactly (K_p1+K_p2+K_p3)/3, so the canonical hull
has these exact sampled fibers and preserves every anchored inclusion.
Their masses are 400,400,4,4624, giving M=5428. The real fiber at
(p1+p2)/2 is the rectangle with half-widths (101/2,101/2), of volume
10201>M. It is centered, hence E=V at its center and
f_H=sqrt(10201/5428)>1 there. The only scalar representation relation
is the affine barycentric relation at p0, so this example also has the
representation-preserving/affine property. No bad-depth claim is made.

## 4. Compact active menus and actual finite groups

The right quantile inequality has the correct orientation. A deepest
source satisfies N.Y-epsilon f(Y)Gamma(u)<=c_Q(N). A proper own critical
cut makes any strictly larger threshold lose positive mass, so equality
holds for its actual mass-Q cap.

The finite clipping construction fixes all base evaluations in a bounded
window and preserves saturated full/empty traces outside it. A minimum-
norm feasible representative is controlled by a pseudoinverse of an
independent subset of finitely many fixed base rows. Proper own cuts make
the preserved thresholds remain the RIGHT Q-quantiles. Thus the local
active quantile set is genuinely compact even when the originally chosen
base tilts diverge. With the pure-base gap, an active nonvertical menu
exists and Caratheodory applies to its continuous supergradients.

Strict own concavity rules out two deepest marks in one fiber: at their
midpoint a proper active quantile would violate the strict averaged
inequality. This uses attained proper caps, which the clipping and core
arguments have already provided; it is not a circular uniqueness premise.

For the full supergradient (alpha,g), the supporting base vector is
sum rho a-epsilon alpha, not sum rho a. Its outward sign and the face
vanishing produce psi>=0 on every assigned fiber. At deepest marks the
weighted quantile slacks are <=0, so all are zero. Strict own concavity
then gives exactly one zero per assigned fiber, including exclusion of
an additional boundary zero. Maximal occupied faces admit integer
relative-interior witnesses; equal parity would create an integer midpoint
in their join face, contradicting maximality. Thus there are at most
k(I)<=k(P) actual groups, with finite old contact sets.

## 5. The signed physical field really produces admissible bodies

For each normal u, Phi(u,z,x) is globally finite convex in (z,x) and
continuous jointly. Compactness in u gives a uniform affine lower bound
-C(1+|x|) at the finite sampled z. Testing the constraint with u=x/|x|
then bounds every new point for tC<1. On this fixed ball Phi is uniformly
bounded. The constraints imply K_z(t) is within O(t) of K_z and contains
an inward homothet about an old inball center. Hence it remains a positive
compact convex body for both inward and outward portions of its speed.

Convexity of Phi and actual old support compatibility prove every sampled
anchored inclusion for the new bodies. Their canonical hull therefore has
these exact sampled fibers, and completeness preserves the same base.
At regular old boundary points the limiting active constraint normal is
the unique old outer normal; radial comparison gives the claimed inward
speed Phi(n,z,x). The inball and O(t) bounds give the dominated radial
hypotheses of the signed energy-envelope theorem. Finite nonnegative sums
of fields are realized simultaneously by the same formula. Signed normal
velocities and optional signed log-scale changes are independently feasible.
Thus the response cone is actually addable; no arbitrary surface-speed
array is being substituted for it.

## 6. Contact minima and branch equalization

The exact group contact minimum localizes to the finite old zeros because
old contacts give O(t), whereas continuity leaves a fixed positive gap
away from them. All nearby minimizing marks lie in fixed interior cores.
The signed energy expansion is uniform there, as are the ordinary volume
and covariance expansions. Nonnegativity of the old psi gives the lower
first-derivative bound; testing the finitely many old marks gives the
upper bound. Therefore alpha'(0+) is precisely the minimum of the stated
contact coefficients. No derivative of a moving deepest mark is needed.

The exact common-quantile equation is locally soluble and unique because
each cap has positive own coarea. It proves a cover of the ENTIRE assigned
new fibers, not just their continued marks. The finite old off-I gap
persists by all-normal continuity, so improvement in every group is a
genuine global upper-bound improvement.

For the conservative cap response R_j^0, deleting the nonnegative inside
hinge leaves a lower loss. Its outside hinge is exactly the infimum over
one measurable selector tau_j in [0,1], shared between its body, threshold,
and moment terms. Every branch has T_j>=S_min>0. Given a direction, solve
the conservative common-loss inverse equation. Every fixed branch
majorizes each R_j^0; monotonic inversion shows its equalized group loss
majorizes the conservative group loss. Choosing the actual hinge signs
at those solved thresholds gives equality for all caps simultaneously.
Taking the minimum contact coefficient is compatible with this argument
because the equalized loss is increasing in the scalar contact budget.
Thus equation (8) is the exact infimum of the compact linear branch family,
with the correct quantifier order. It is not a choice of separate physical
motions or separate cap weights for each row.

## 7. A literal compact coefficient space for ONE separator

Here is the compact-space formulation implicit in Section 6 of the cover
note. Let T_i be the product over its finitely many cap faces of the
weak-star-compact sets {tau in L-infinity:0<=tau<=1}. Include a finite
contact label a. Let X be the finite DISJOINT union of these contact × T_i
spaces, over all groups i. It is a compact Hausdorff space. Each branch
functional evaluated on one physical/normal/scale direction is continuous
on X: all speeds and moments are integrable against the finite old face
measure, selector pairings are weak-star continuous, and all T_j and B_i
stay bounded away from zero. Put Prob(X) in its usual weak topology;
this is compact.

For any finite list of physical fields, include every signed normal
coordinate and, when used, both signed scale coordinates. The admissible
finite response cone is convex. No simultaneous strict improvement means
its downward concave hypograph misses the open positive orthant. Separate
them. Equivalently, the compact convex hull of the finite-dimensional branch
coefficient vectors intersects the negative polar of the actual finite
cone; otherwise strict separation and approximation from that cone give
an actual strict improvement. This yields a probability measure in Prob(X)
whose averaged branch functional is nonpositive on every listed physical
field and zero on signed coordinates.

For a fixed physical test these averaged inequalities define CLOSED
subsets of Prob(X). Every finite intersection is nonempty by the preceding
finite response argument, and all signed coordinates can be included in
every finite list. Compactness therefore gives one probability measure
satisfying every physical test at once. No fixed finite support is claimed
for this eventual measure; finite support is available only for each
finite-dimensional restriction. That distinction avoids an invalid
infinite-dimensional use of Caratheodory.

The reconstruction of kappa, omega and the effective outside selectors
is valid under this ONE measure. In particular integrating
omega-branch times T_j gives rho_j times the corresponding contact-force
sum, and the same outside selector enters the body and section moments.
The total omega mass is one, so 0<=W<=1. The source, covariance, and
cap parts of A are positive. Affine fields and their negatives give the
claimed conditional normal masses and first moments; convex physical
tests then give the stated surface convex order. This is still a
surface-to-surface law, not a source-to-original-volume martingale.

## 8. Scope

The finite-intersection proof supplies a separator for the declared
normal-dependent convex-field cone with the fixed conservative inside-zero
branch, arbitrary signed cap-normal velocities, and optional signed scale.
It does not supply one separator simultaneously over all possible inside
branches, arbitrary nonconvex physical fields, reoptimized old menus, or
free concave parameters. The source claims none of those stronger facts.

The ordinary energy/concavity theorem and original minimal-bad-base
reduction remain named analytic/geometric inputs. Within those inputs,
the new H-specific attainment, finite-cover continuation, conservative
branch infimum, and ONE-separator construction have passed this audit.
The missing Gamma/outside-capacity comparison remains separate.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
